messages:
ravi: Quick note from support: new user tried the quickstart curl example and kept getting 401s. Turns out the README shows `Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY` (literally) instead of the env var expansion example.

lina: oh yikes. do we have the curl snippet in multiple places?

ravi: yes, quickstart top-level and the tutorials page. current example: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

should be either: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` or show the export step above.

henry: also saw mismatch in Java: the README uses `new Redwood()` but the latest Java SDK uses `RedwoodClient.builder().apiKey(System.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")).build()` — we should standardize across languages to use the canonical env var name.

lina: good catch. i'll patch the curl and Java snippets. can someone add a one-line test that greps for `REDWOOD_KEY` in the docs repo?

ravi: i added a small QA check in my branch that fails the docs build if deprecated env var names are present. linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/401

docs-bot: docs build check: found 2 matches for "REDWOOD_KEY" in quickstart and tutorials.

qa-bot: ran sample smoke tests: quickstart containers started, curl returned 401 expected for fake key; smoke test verifies presence of example export lines.

henry: while updating Java, i also included a short note about retry settings using the SDK helper: `RedwoodClient.builder().retries(4).backoffMillis(150).build()` so the JVM example matches Node/Python docs.

lina: thanks. i'll also add a sentence in CONTRIBUTING: "When changing auth variable names or client constructors, update all language quickstarts and run grep-check before merging."

ravi: assigning follow-ups: @lina (merge curl/java fixes), @henry (add retry snippet), @ravi (maintain grep QA check).

lina: will merge after CI. :thumbsup:

ravi: small but high-impact. onboarding wins!

henry: great teamwork.
